title: AI Inside an AI: Internal RL w/ Temporal Abstraction
summary: Discover AI summary of Google's 'emergent temporal abstraction' direction: a decoder-only transformer is augmented with an internal meta-controller that reads and steers the residual stream, stores long-horizon plans in a GRU-style latent state, and reduces sparse-reward search into a lower-dimensional skill-selection problem.
claims: Standard token-level reinforcement learning struggles on long-horizon reasoning because sparse rewards and large token search spaces cause poor credit assignment.
A frozen base transformer can be treated as an environment while a smaller internal meta-controller learns to monitor and steer intermediate activations.
The proposed controller uses a recurrent latent state to preserve strategic context beyond the base model's effective context window.
Low-rank steering of the residual stream is presented as a way to constrain intervention to meaningful subspaces instead of injecting unconstrained high-dimensional noise.
The architecture is framed as enabling compositional reuse of learned skills, improving exploration and temporal credit assignment without requiring full retraining of the base model.
